title: Cyber-Jcode full pentest engagement mode
highlights: New [10] Full pentest mode: seven ordered methodology phases (recon, services, web, vulns, exploit, privesc, post) running toward the highest privilege
Live per-tool streaming during phases: every tool invocation and result is shown as it completes, bash commands shown with their command line
Plain corporate English DOCX engagement report with evidence screenshots, per-phase methodology table, findings with evidence-linked validation, and a full recorded-tool appendix
improvements: Phase transitions: Enter/y run the next phase, n stops and reports, s skips that phase
Ctrl+C mid-phase keeps partial tool outputs, records the phase as partial, and still produces the report
Phase results travel forward as engagement context; verified flags persist across phases
Pentest policy contract adds structured [CYBER_FINDINGS] with asset, reproduction and evidence excerpts, plus verified access-level reporting
Installer copies the user's pentest handbooks into ~/.cyber-jcode/references (once, never overwritten); phases reference them as methodology guidance
Report renderer: simple black/white corporate styling, page-safe evidence images, command + output per tool in Appendix A
fixes: Skip ('s') now actually skips the next phase instead of running it
Robust phase context assembly when a phase report lacks a phase key
Report building tolerates missing engagement fields and never crashes a finished engagement
